reason: The cited lines show the handler requesting browser console logs via a socket message, serializing them, and returning them as text. This does not show arbitrary host code execution. It also does not show sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; the socket message is fixed and empty. Console log contents are page-controlled/browser content, so the returned data can be attacker-controllable, supporting UNTRUSTED. The lines do not establish that the logs contain non-public host files, databases, credentialed SaaS data, or localhost/intranet content, so SECRET is insufficient.
